steps.title: Draw a bar for each class

steps.title: Compare the renewable column with Ireland

lines.text: Ireland used $6\%$ renewable energy. Look for countries below 6: Cyprus 5, Luxembourg 4, Malta 2, Netherlands 4.
Bulgaria (8) and France (7) are above 6, so they do not count. Denmark is also excluded because its renewable value from (b)(i) is 20, which is above 6.

lines.text: Cyprus and Malta both show 0 for gas, so either is correct.

steps.title: Draw the sectors one after another

lines.text: Start from the radius at the end of the renewable sector (the $22^\circ$ line).
Using a protractor, measure each angle anticlockwise and draw a radius: oil $151^\circ$, solid fuel $47^\circ$, gas $86^\circ$, then electricity $54^\circ$.
The angles add to $22 + 151 + 47 + 86 + 54 = 360^\circ$, so the last radius closes back onto the starting line.
Label each sector with its energy type.

steps.title: Sort the ages by their tens digit

lines.text: The stem is the tens digit and the leaf is the units digit. Go through the 28 ages in order and put each leaf on its stem.

steps.title: Write each stem in increasing order

lines.text: Put the leaves in order, smallest first, on each row.
Check: $3+4+7+5+5+4 = 28$ leaves, one for every employee.

steps.title: Use the statistics mode on the calculator

lines.text: Enter the speeds as the $x$ values and the fuel consumption as the $y$ values.
Read off the correlation coefficient $r$.

steps.title: Compare the two tests

lines.text: Every student swam further in the re-test than in the initial test, so everyone improved.
The improvements were not equal: 22 m rose by 3 m, but 61 m rose by 289 m.
The points curve upwards, not along a straight line, so the stronger swimmers improved by much more than the weaker ones.

steps.title: Find r with the calculator

lines.text: Enter the initial test distances as $x$ and the re-test distances as $y$ in statistics mode, then read the correlation coefficient.

steps.title: Find the sums needed

lines.text: Let $x$ be city and $y$ be motorway, with $n = 8$ cars.

steps.title: Evaluate the top of the formula

lines.text: $r = \dfrac{n\sum xy - \sum x \sum y}{\sqrt{\left(n\sum x^2 - (\sum x)^2\right)\left(n\sum y^2 - (\sum y)^2\right)}}$

steps.title: Evaluate the bottom of the formula
Calculate r
Explain why r can be close to 0 in part (b)

lines.text: The correlation coefficient measures how well the points fit a straight line. These points follow a quadratic (U-shaped) curve, which is symmetrical, so no straight line fits them and $r_{FS}$ is close to 0.

candidates.final: r = 0.966;\ \text{correlation measures linear relationships, and this data is quadratic}

steps.title: (i) List the red cubes and find their total

lines.text: Red cubes per trial (A to G): $0, 3, 2, 2, 4, 5, 1$.

steps.title: (i) Find the mean
(i) Find the sum of the squares of the red values
(i) Find the variance

lines.text: Use $\sigma^2 = \dfrac{\sum x^2}{n} - \bar{x}^2$.

steps.title: (i) Find the standard deviation
(ii) Set up the correlation calculation

lines.text: Let $x$ be the red cubes and $y$ the green cubes, with $n = 7$. Green cubes per trial: $4, 2, 0, 3, 0, 0, 2$.

steps.title: (ii) Substitute into the correlation formula

lines.tex: r &= \frac{n\sum xy - \sum x \sum y}{\sqrt{\left(n\sum x^2 - (\sum x)^2\right)\left(n\sum y^2 - (\sum y)^2\right)}}

steps.title: (iii) Explain why the correlation is negative

lines.text: Each trial picks exactly $5$ cubes, so the red, green and blue counts always add to $5$.
If a trial has more red cubes, there is less room for green cubes, so fewer green cubes are likely.
As the number of red cubes increases, the number of green cubes tends to decrease, so the correlation coefficient is negative.

skill.title: Estimate the mean of grouped data

steps.title: Find the mid-interval value of each group

lines.text: Mid-value = (lower end + upper end) $\div 2$.

steps.title: Multiply each mid-value by its percentage and add

lines.text: The percentages add to 100, so divide the total by 100.

steps.title: Find the mid-interval values

lines.text: The mid-interval value is halfway between the ends of each class, e.g. $\frac{145+150}{2} = 147.5$.

steps.title: Multiply each frequency by its mid-value
Add up the products and the frequencies
Divide to find the mean
Find the mid-interval value of each class

lines.text: Add the ends of each interval and halve: $24$–$30$ gives $27$, $30$–$36$ gives $33$, $36$–$42$ gives $39$.

steps.title: Find the sum of (mid-value × frequency)
Find the total number of people
Set mean = 40.4 and solve for k

lines.text: The mean is $\sum fx$ divided by $\sum f$.

Draw the line of best fit by eye

The mean point is $(72,\ 14.9)$, and the slope is about $-0.15$, so the line runs from about $(40,\ 19.7)$ to $(112,\ 8.9)$.

steps.title: Plot car G

lines.text: Car G has city 30 and motorway 40, so plot the point $(30, 40)$ and label it G.

steps.title: Plot car H

lines.text: Car H has city 17 and motorway 30, so plot the point $(17, 30)$ and label it H.

steps.title: Draw the line of best fit by eye

lines.text: Draw one straight line through the middle of the points, with some points above it and some below, rising from left to right.
The line shown passes through $(20, 31)$ and $(50, 61)$.

candidates.final: G(30, 40),\ H(17, 30)\text{ and a line of best fit}

steps.title: Estimate the motorway value for K

lines.text: K has city 20. Go up from 20 on the city axis to the line of best fit, then across to the motorway axis. This reads about 31.

steps.title: Estimate the city value for L

lines.text: L has motorway 60. Go across from 60 on the motorway axis to the line of best fit, then down to the city axis. This reads about 49.

steps.title: Decide which estimate to trust

lines.text: K is more reliable. A city value of 20 lies inside the range of the data (15 to 30), so the estimate is interpolation.
L is well beyond all of the given data points, so the line is being extended into a region with no evidence (extrapolation).

candidates.final: K \approx 31,\ L \approx 49;\ \text{more confident in K, as L is well beyond the data}

steps.title: Work out the interquartile range
Use the median

lines.text: With 8 numbers the median is the mean of $D$ and $E$.

steps.title: Use the lower quartile

lines.text: The lower quartile is the median of $A, B, C, D$, which is the mean of $B$ and $C$.

steps.title: Use the interquartile range

lines.text: The upper quartile is the mean of $F$ and $G$.

steps.title: Use the mean

lines.tex: A + B + C + D + E + F + G + H &= 8 \times 13.5
A + B + C + D + E + F + G + H &= 108

steps.title: Use the range
Split D + E and B + C

lines.text: $D + E = 25$ with $D < E$ and a gap of at least 2: $D = 12, E = 13$ fails (gap 1) and $D = 10, E = 15$ fails because $F = 16$ is only 1 above 15. So $D = 11$, $E = 14$.

$B + C = 15$ with $C \le 9$ (a gap of at least 2 below $D = 11$) and $B \ge 6$ (a gap of at least 2 above $A = 4$): $B = 6$, $C = 9$. (B = 7, C = 8 is not allowed because $C$ must be at least 2 more than $B$, so $C \ge B + 2$. With $B + C = 15$ this gives $B \le 6.5$, and with $B \ge 6$ this forces $B = 6$.)
